learning_outcomes.text: Provide knowledge on methods for schematizing simple mechanical systems and for evaluating stress states.
Provide knowledge on the mechanical properties of materials and methods for dimensioning and verifying components subjected to static and fatigue loads.
Provide knowledge on the main machine elements used in the design of mechanical systems and on design, selection, and verification methodologies.
Apply design elements to individual machine components.
Understand and assemble components to achieve the design of machines and assemblies.
Design, select, and verify the main machine elements used in the creation of simple mechanical systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to concepts of probability and reliability
Materials. Generalities and reminders on characteristics and properties of metallic materials. Uses
Reminders of statics. Isostatic structures. Stress characteristics. Stress state of beams. Calculation of stresses
Complements of Statics. Principal stresses. Stress concentration states. Hertzian contact. Eulerian instability. Curved beams. Deformations and stiffnesses
Static loading conditions. Resistance criteria for yielding and fracture of ductile and brittle materials

Fatigue loading conditions. Fatigue behavior of materials (S-N). Factors influencing the fatigue strength of components and machines. Reliability in fatigue. High-cycle fatigue design. Damage accumulation and load spectra. Hertzian fatigue
Structural connections. Principles of force transfer. Forced connections. Dismountable connections. Non-dismountable connections
Shaft-hub connections. Keys, splines, and grooved profiles
assessment_rules: The written exam is passed if the evaluation is 18/30 or higher. Students who pass the written exam are admitted to the oral exam. A positively evaluated written exam is not considered and remains valid for subsequent sessions if the student does not pass the oral exam.
